info.title: @mintopia/harmonic
info.description:
Queue, run, and review autonomous coding-agent tasks over ACP

## MCP

`POST /mcp` is a stateless streamable-HTTP MCP server (not a REST
endpoint, so it has no entry in this spec's paths). It authenticates the
same way as the REST API — a bearer token, either an operator API key or
the Run Key Harmonic injects into a spawned harness — and exposes the
agent task surface as MCP tools (task CRUD, dependencies, queue/cancel,
runs and events). Accept/Reject are human-only and are never exposed as
MCP tools — a verifier's pass is the accept (#140, ADR-0021). A run-scoped
Run Key may call `/mcp` regardless of the REST restrictions noted per
endpoint below. Work Context lease diagnostics/supersede/unlock
(`list_leases`, `supersede_lease`, `unlock_lease`, issue #125) are
operator-only tools, the same footing as Accept/Reject: a Run Key can call
`/mcp` but gets a `forbidden` error from these three specifically — only
an operator API key (`scope: 'full'`) or an authenticated session may call
them.

## WebSocket

`GET /api/ws` is a single firehose WebSocket (also outside this spec's
paths): every run event, run state change, task state change/removal, and
Conversation event/change is broadcast to every connected client as JSON
messages of the form `{ type: 'run_event' | 'run_changed' | 'run_usage' |
'task_changed' | 'task_removed' | 'conversation_event' | 'conversation_changed' |
'permission_request', ... }`, using the same Task/Run/Conversation shapes
served over REST. `run_usage` is a live-usage snapshot for a running Run
(tokens, context fill, derived Cost, current-activity line, and Process
Tree), pushed about once a second while the Run tails its native log.
`task_removed` (issue #162) announces a hard-deleted Task's id (`{ type:
'task_removed', id }`) — the row is gone, not another state change.
`permission_request` announces a Harness blocked on an
operator permission decision in a Conversation (ADR-0007), answered via
`POST /conversations/:id/permissions/:reqId`. Authenticate by passing the
session token or an API key as `?token=` (WebSocket clients cannot set an
Authorization header). A `read`-scoped key gets a filtered firehose — only
`task_changed`, `task_removed`, `run_changed`, `run_event`, and
`run_usage` — with the Conversation and permission traffic dropped.

## Read scope

A `read`-scoped API key (created via `POST /api/keys` with
`{ "scope": "read" }`) is a viz-client credential: it may `GET` tasks,
runs, maps, and the instance-wide Activity snapshot (`/api/activity`,
filtered to Runs only for a read key), and open the WebSocket (filtered as
above). Every mutation and the whole operator surface (keys, config,
channels, Conversations) is blocked. There is no `map_changed` event — a
client re-fetches `/maps` on reconnect or when it sees a `mapRef` it has
not resolved yet.

409.description: The task is running or finished, so its definition is frozen.

delete.description: Permanently delete a Task and its Runs, Usage, and Dependency edges. A mirrored Task is also dismissed so a re-poll will not re-create it. Distinct from Cancel, which keeps the record.

200.description: The id of the deleted Task.

schema.description: The id of the deleted Task.

post.description: Promote a draft to ready (or blocked, if dependencies are unmet). Reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

post.description: Cancel a non-terminal task, optionally cascading to its dependents. Reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

200.description: The task in its new state.

409.description: The task is not in a state this action can be applied to.

post.description: Force a running task to completed (operator override): stop the agent and settle it done, skipping the review gate. Operator only.

200.description: The task in its new state.

409.description: The task is not running.

post.description: Steer a running task: send an operator message to its active run. When the harness supports ACP mid-turn steering, the message is injected into the running turn immediately — pre-empting the current generation without cancelling it. Otherwise, or when the agent is parked between turns, the message is queued and delivered as a fresh prompt turn at the next turn boundary. Use it to redirect an agent that has gone off-track, or to nudge one that ended its turn and parked. Operator only.

text.example: Stop — check the existing tests before changing the limiter.

200.description: The message was injected into the running turn, or queued for the next turn boundary, of the task's active run.

409.description: The task has no active run to steer (it is not running here).

post.description: Un-escalate a mirrored Task: clear the escalated flag and flip drive back to afk, handing it back to autonomous drive. The Task keeps its state (usually ready), so the Auto-Runner re-picks it. Operator only.

200.description: The Task, no longer escalated and back on afk drive.

409.description: The Task is native, or is not escalated.

post.description: Send a failed task back to ready for another attempt, with optional feedback for the retry. Native tasks append it to the prompt; mirrored tasks carry it in the feedback field (their prompt is re-derived from the ticket each poll). Reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

409.description: The task is not in a state this action can be applied to.

post.description: Return a cancelled task to the queue in place: ready, or blocked if it has unmet dependencies. Reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

200.description: The task in its new state.

409.description: The task is not cancelled.

post.description: Create a new task that re-attempts an existing one: a copy of its config and dependencies, linked back via reattemptOf, carrying optional reviewer feedback (composed into the run prompt at run time, so the original prompt stays pristine). The original is left unchanged. Reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

409.description: Only a failed or rejected task can be re-attempted.

409.description: The edge is unknown, self-referential, or would close a dependency cycle.

409.description: The task is not in a state this action can be applied to.

get.description: The derived Map rollup: every Map from the last tracker poll with its member Tasks and per-state counts, each stamped with its Workspace. `?workspaceId=` scopes to one Workspace's board (issue #45). Query-time (no table); empty when tracker mirroring is off or before the first poll. Reachable with a read-scoped API Key.

schema.description: Every derived Map, newest tracker scan.

post.description: Create a Conversation (an interactive, multi-turn exchange the operator drives with a Harness over ACP). Execution settings default from global config. Operator only; not reachable with a run-scoped key. The harness spawns on the first Turn, not here.

201.description: The created Conversation, active and awaiting its first Turn.

400.description: The payload failed validation, or the requested harness is not configured on this server.

get.description: List Conversations, newest first, optionally scoped to one Workspace. Operator only; not reachable with a run-scoped key.

200.description: Every matching Conversation, active and ended alike, newest first.

post.description: Send an operator Turn. Spawns the harness on the first Turn and keeps it warm across Turns; the reply streams over the WebSocket. If a Turn is already running, the message is queued and sent as the next Turn (issue 14). Operator only; not reachable with a run-scoped key.

text.example: Why does the rate limiter drop the first request after a restart?

schema.description: The Turn was accepted; `queued` says whether it went behind a running one.

400.description: The payload failed validation, or the harness could not be spawned — its Working Directory does not exist, or its harness is not configured.

409.description: The Conversation has ended, so it can take no further Turns.

post.description: Steer a running Turn (issue 14): cancel the in-flight Turn via ACP session/cancel and re-prompt with `text` as the next Turn, or just stop it when `text` is empty. The cancelled Turn records a cancelled stop reason. Operator only; not reachable with a run-scoped key.

text.example: Stop — check the existing tests first.

200.description: The in-flight Turn was cancelled, and any steering text queued as the next.

400.description: The payload failed validation, or steering an idle Conversation could not spawn the harness — its Working Directory does not exist, or its harness is not configured.

409.description: The Conversation has ended, so it has no Turn to steer.

post.description: Answer a Harness's held permission request in a Conversation (ADR-0007). `optionId` is the ACP option the operator chose — allow_once, the native allow_always ('Allow for this conversation'), or a reject option. Set `remember` to also persist a Permission Rule ('Always allow in {dir}') keyed on the tool kind + Working Directory. Operator only; not reachable with a run-scoped key.

200.description: The answer was handed to the Harness and the held request released.

404.description: No permission request with that reqId is pending for this Conversation.

post.description: End a Conversation: stop the harness and mark it ended (its transcript survives read-only; it cannot resume). Operator only; not reachable with a run-scoped key.

200.description: The Conversation in its ended state; already-ended is a no-op.

get.description: List persistent Permission Rules (auto-approve a tool kind in a Working Directory across Conversations). Operator only; not reachable with a run-scoped key.

200.description: Every Permission Rule in force, newest first.

schema.description: Every Permission Rule in force, newest first.

delete.description: Revoke a Permission Rule; matching requests prompt again afterwards. Operator only; not reachable with a run-scoped key.

200.description: The rule was revoked; requests it used to auto-approve prompt again.

404.description: No Permission Rule has that id.

get.description: Get the full effective configuration. Operator only; not reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

200.description: The stored configuration in full: harnesses, price overrides, defaults, auto-runner settings, and flags.

prompt.example: Review the diff for correctness against the ticket.

patch.description: Deep-merge a partial config patch onto the stored configuration. Operator only; not reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

200.description: The whole configuration as stored once the patch was merged onto it.

prompt.example: Review the diff for correctness against the ticket.

schema.description: The whole configuration as stored once the patch was merged onto it.

put.description: Full-replace the stored configuration. Unlike PATCH's deep-merge, a record key omitted here (a harness env var, a price override) is deleted, not left alone — the settings UI loads the whole config, edits locally, and saves the complete object so it can delete as well as add. Validated atomically against the config schema: an invalid body is rejected with no partial write. Operator only; not reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

prompt.example: Review the diff for correctness against the ticket.

200.description: The whole configuration as stored after the replace, with omitted optional fields filled from the schema's defaults.

prompt.example: Review the diff for correctness against the ticket.

schema.description: The whole configuration as stored after the replace, with omitted optional fields filled from the schema's defaults.

post.description: Log in with the operator password, starting a session cookie.

200.description: The password matched; a session cookie is set on this response.

401.description: The password did not match, or no operator password has been set yet.

post.description: End the current session.

200.description: The cookie is cleared and its session destroyed; sent the same way when there was no session to end.

get.description: Whether the caller has a valid session, and whether an operator password has been set.

200.description: Whether this request's cookie names a live session, and whether an operator password is configured at all.

schema.description: Whether this request's cookie names a live session, and whether an operator password is configured at all.

post.description: Set or change the operator password. When one is already set, currentPassword must match (a wrong current password changes nothing); when none is set (ungated), currentPassword is ignored and this sets the initial password. newPassword takes the same minimum-length rule as initial setup. On success every session other than the caller's own is destroyed — a stolen cookie doesn't survive a credential rotation — but API Keys are untouched. Operator only; not reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

200.description: The password was changed; every session other than the caller's own is now destroyed, and API Keys are untouched.

400.description: newPassword is shorter than the four-character minimum, or the payload was otherwise invalid — nothing was changed.

401.description: The request carried no valid session or key, or currentPassword did not match — nothing was changed.

delete.description: Remove the operator password — Harmonic falls back to ungated (every API surface open). Verifies currentPassword first when one is set; a no-op when none is set (idempotent). On success every session other than the caller's own is destroyed. Operator only; not reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

200.description: The password is removed (or was already unset); Harmonic is now ungated.

401.description: A password is set and currentPassword did not match — nothing was changed.

post.description: Create a new operator API key. `scope` defaults to 'full' (drives the whole fleet); 'read' mints a viz-client key that can GET tasks/runs/maps and open the WebSocket but cannot mutate anything. The bearer token is returned once and never stored.

201.description: The created key, with its bearer token in `token` — the only response that ever carries it.

schema.description: The created key, with its bearer token in `token` — the only response that ever carries it.

get.description: List operator API keys (Run Keys are internal and never listed).

200.description: Every full-scope operator key, revoked ones included, newest first; no token values.

schema.description: Every full-scope operator key, revoked ones included, newest first; no token values.

delete.description: Revoke an operator API key immediately.

200.description: The key can no longer authenticate; re-revoking an already-revoked key keeps its original revokedAt.

get.description: Usage, Cost, and run-state counts over a time range (by run start time). Operator only; not reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

200.description: Usage, Cost, and run-state counts over the runs started in the range; totals and Cost count only what the runs actually reported and could be priced, so they are floors wherever `incomplete` is true.

schema.description: Usage, Cost, and run-state counts over the runs started in the range; totals and Cost count only what the runs actually reported and could be priced, so they are floors wherever `incomplete` is true.

get.description: Instance-wide snapshot of every live process across Workspaces (ADR 0010): in-flight Runs and warm Conversations from the in-memory registries, each joined with its latest Usage, context fill, derived Cost, and (Runs only) current-activity line and Process Tree. The Activity view loads this once on page-load, then follows the live `run_usage` firehose. A Read Key (a read-scoped API key) sees Runs only — Conversations are excluded, matching the firehose filter.

200.description: Every live process across Workspaces (Runs then Conversations); an empty array when nothing is running. Unordered beyond that — the Activity view applies its own attention ranking.

schema.description: Every live process across Workspaces (Runs then Conversations); an empty array when nothing is running. Unordered beyond that — the Activity view applies its own attention ranking.

post.description: Create a notification channel. Operator only; not reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

201.description: The created channel; events falls back to the default subscriptions when omitted.

400.description: The payload failed validation, or the config does not match the shape the channel's type requires.

get.description: List notification channels. Operator only; not reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

200.description: Every configured notification channel.

schema.description: Every configured notification channel.

get.description: Get one notification channel. Operator only; not reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

200.description: Every channel id now overridden for the task; adding an override that is already set changes nothing.

200.description: Every channel id still overridden for the task; removing an override that was not set is a no-op.

schema.description: Every channel id still overridden for the task; removing an override that was not set is a no-op.

get.description: Immediate child directories of `path`, one level deep — the data behind the workspace directory picker (issue #62). An empty or omitted `path` starts at the server user's home. Files and hidden (dot) directories are excluded; entries are sorted by name. No root restriction — any directory the running user can read is browsable (a sysadmin concern, per the map decision). Operator-only: a full-scope session is required (not reachable with a scoped or read key).

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Absolute path to browse; defaults to the server user home.

200.description: The browsed path, its parent, and its immediate child directories.

400.description: The path is not a directory, or the running user cannot read it.

get.description: List every Work Context lease with operator diagnostics: owner Run/Task, TTL state, and the ready Tasks queued behind it. Operator only.

200.description: Every held or suspect lease, with its queue diagnostics.

schema.description: Every held or suspect lease, with its queue diagnostics.

post.description: Re-point a stuck lease to a Run the operator names, re-admitting it as held with a fresh TTL — the escape for a suspect lease reconciliation could not resolve on its own. Operator only.

200.description: The lease now belongs to the named Run.

404.description: No lease is held for that key, or no Run has that id.

post.description: Force-release a lease outright, freeing its key for a fresh acquire — use when no Run should inherit the stuck context. Operator only.

200.description: The lease was released; the key is free for a fresh acquire.

404.description: No lease is held for that key.

post.description: Force-land an Epic's ready subset: merge whatever is folded into its integration branch into the default branch now, bypassing the all-members-completed gate — but not Verification, which still gates the merge. Operator only.

200.description: The force-land attempt's outcome.

409.description: No active whole-Epic land coordinator for this Workspace (tracking is off or the loop has not started).
